column1: # extdisk-apfs host catalogue. Tab-separated, twelve fields, one application or
# tool per line. tests/run validates every line, so a malformed one fails CI.
# id        kebab-case, unique. This is what `host --only` takes.
# name      what to show a person
#           full    the whole data directory or library can live on the volume
#           partial only a cache, a build directory or a media folder can
#           none    nothing can, and the setting field says why
# kind      cli | env | ui | flag | file | none
#           cli  a command of the tool writes the setting persistently
#           env  an environment variable the tool documents
#           ui   a setting inside a graphical application
#           flag a per-invocation flag, so there is nothing to persist
#           file a key in a configuration file, with no command to write it
# subdir    directory to create on the volume, or - when the app makes its own
# setting   cli:  an argv template, space-separated, %s for the path
#           flag: the flag as you would type it, %s for the path
#           ui:   the steps, as one sentence, %s for the path
#           file: the key and the file to put it in, %s for the path
#           none: the reason nothing can move
# query     cli: an argv template that prints the current value, otherwise -
# revert    cli: an argv template that undoes the setting, otherwise -
# source    where the claim comes from: a command, a man page, or a URL
# note      a requirement or a consequence worth knowing, or -
# `host` applies the cli and env rows and creates the directories. It prints
# the flag, file and ui rows, because nothing persistent exists to write.
# A row with no verified source does not belong in this file.
